title: How Ruben Hassid turns his voice into a text file any AI can use
summary: Ruben argues your voice, taste and judgment are patterns that compress into one markdown file. He shares a two-prompt workflow: a 100-question AI interview, then a compression pass into a lean about-me file. Reuse it across Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and teammates, and keep editing it.

principles.text: Your voice, taste and habits are patterns, so they can be captured in one text file any AI can read.
principles.quote: Patterns. Every one of them is a pattern.

principles.text: Extract your voice via a 100-question AI interview; dictate answers by voice, which is faster and more honest.
principles.quote: Voice is faster and more honest.

principles.text: Compress the raw interview dump into a lean file, since a bloated file eats context window and costs tokens every turn.
principles.quote: But this file is too big. It eats too much of your context window.

principles.text: Keep only lines that change AI behavior. Cut generic values, flattery and biography; keep specifics, refusals and examples.
principles.quote: Optimize for maximum behavioral fidelity per token.

principles.text: Make the file portable: reuse it in any model and hand it to your team or ghostwriter so they draft in your voice.
principles.quote: You’re now a resource instead of a bottleneck.

principles.text: Do the hard work once to gain consistency, but edit the file often because your taste keeps changing.
